title: What do you guys think AI is going to do to gaming in the next 10 years?
author: Melolibya
selftext:
Hey everyone, what do you guys think AI is going to do to gaming in the next 10 years?

Honestly, I never really cared that much about AI before. I used to think a lot of the stuff people were saying about AI was kinda silly, like  AI will do this" or  AI will do that" and I just didn't believe it was possible.

But damn, the last 2 years really changed my whole perspective on it.

Just seeing how much AI improved recently is crazy. Last month especially, seeing what GPT 6 Astra was able to do honestly shocked me. Stuff that I thought was years away suddenly feels way closer than I expected.

And it made me think about gaming.

I feel like AI could completely change gaming over the next 10 years. Not just help developers make games faster, but actually change what games can be.

For example, right now making a big game takes hundreds of people and years of work. But if AI keeps improving, maybe in the future a small team or even a single person could make something that would normally require a huge studio.

Of course, we're probably going to get A LOT of garbage too lol. There will probably be an insane amount of AI slop and terrible games.

But at the same time, if everyone has the tools to make games, there should also be way more good and creative games. People will be able to make games that would never get approved or funded by a big publisher.

And the thing I'm most interested in is AI actually being inside the games.

Imagine an RPG or MMO where NPCs aren't just following the same 5 dialogue options. Every NPC actually has their own personality, memories, relationships and goals.

You help some random NPC at the beginning of the game and 50 hours later they still remember you. Maybe they become your friend, maybe they hate you, maybe they tell other people about what you did.

Or imagine a whole world where NPCs are actually doing their own thing even when you're not around.

That's the kind of thing that could make an MMO feel like an actual living world instead of just a huge map full of quest markers.

Something like those isekai anime where the main character gets thrown into another world and everyone there feels like an actual person.

And then there's mods.

Imagine being able to take an old game you love and basically tell AI:  Make me a new story for this game, add new quests, characters and locations but keep the same feeling and gameplay."

Obviously we're nowhere near being able to do that perfectly right now, but I honestly wouldn't be surprised if something like that becomes possible in the next 10 years.

I don't think AI is going to magically make every game amazing. If anything, there will probably be more bad games than ever.

But there could also be WAY more amazing games because the barrier to making them becomes so much lower.

Maybe I'm being too optimistic, but after seeing how much AI changed in just the last couple of years, I don't really feel comfortable saying "that's impossible" anymore.

What do you guys think? Am I being way too optimistic about AI and gaming, or do you think the next 10 years are going to completely change gaming?

comments.author: GreenBlueStar
comments.body: Lots of porn games are in the horizon for sure.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body: I'll say this: I think Epic is suddenly looking very smart turning Unreal into a 'verse' engine.

comments.author: ContactIcy3963
comments.body:
AI will supplant a lot of “average” coders with “good” imagineers.

I think great developers will continue to be better than AI but the floor AI keeps lifting will deservedly crowd out a lot of people who know how to code but can’t make a good game. 

In about a year or so I expect a game to hit top sales on steam made mostly with AI code and art generation. Just needs a good creative person to imagine the game who also has good knowledge of code to bugstomp the context bugs and hallucinations.

replies.author: Discodowns
replies.body: I think those great engineers will just be better at using AI than everyone else

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
>I think great developers will continue to be better than AI

Great developers use AI. There's no "better than".

replies.author: wrong_castle
replies.body:
I’m excited to see what AI does in terms of game engines. I have a hunch that we’re about to see a new era of rapid improvement in tooling. We’re already seeing this.

“I need a tool” to “I built the tool” pipeline is becoming trivialized.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Asian companies already use a lot of AI openly, because it speeds up the processes. So we'll see a lot of new stuff coming from there. Not always good, there will be more slop as well.

replies.author: ContactIcy3963
replies.body: No different than the mobile slop era let alone the video game glut of the early 1980s

replies.author: MYSTONYMOUS
replies.body: I've been coding professionally 25 years. I guarantee you there will not be any great developers left that don't use AI for nearly everything. Instead, great developers will specialize in being the best at using AI tools, getting high quality code and exactly the results they want out of AI, and being able to understand and vet the underlying architecture and guide and pivot the AI as needed to make better architecture. They will also be quick and great code reviewers.

replies.author: ContactIcy3963
replies.body: Yep. Same in finance. Nobody writes the manual macros/SQL anymore. In a way we all became leads and product managers. I shudder for the next generation though. All that manual work is now done by AI

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: I suspect 99,999% of games will be made by people who do not care about games about design and game development at all. They will just flood the market to make money.

comments.author: 12OffIntx
comments.body: The ability to put together a game without strong coding or art skills will do a couple things. It will allow people with original ideas, who never before had the means, to build their dream game(s). It will also be difficult for them to get noticed because AI will enable an avalanche of "I made Minecraft, but with hexagons" unoriginality.  I love the idea of the former, even trying that myself - but I fear the impact of the latter.

comments.author: lovelessBertha
comments.body: Plenty of positive but the big negative is we will enter an unprecedented level of slop shovelware. The Wii will look like the golden age in comparison.

comments.author: k_from_HyperDraw
comments.body:
we already see ai games on topics nobody would care/dare to pick  
there will be more.  
hopeful to see some breakout hits

comments.author: acrolicious
comments.body: Hyper realistic AI characters and companions in Open World RPGs... 😬

comments.author: Victorex123
comments.body:
Triple A companies will make something like Roblox, users could make their own games with the AI tools and other users could play those games.

I see a dark future for small projects made with AI, AAA has more resources to make the thing I said before. So, maybe that will be the way for them.

If the tools make it to see, you can just made your “dream” game or modify one to have all things you like.

comments.author: Slight_Season_4500
comments.body: More bugs and glitches and poorly maintained games

comments.author: TheCatsMeow1022
comments.body: Maybe not what people in this community want to hear but my opinion is we won’t even need game devs sometime in the not so distant future. Anybody will be able to create what they want when they want it.

replies.author: tilesofthenadirat
replies.body: You can create joke, but still prefer to hear one from a different person. It's more like nobody gonna pay you 70 bucks for that joke. So I foretell price drop in games.

comments.author: master_internutter
comments.body: NPCs are all going to have human level intelligence

comments.author: Ethrealrunner
comments.body: There was an article on a patent from Microsoft for an active AI that can change the gamestate as you play.  Increasing the stuff it sees you spending more time doing.  Ie. Adventurers get more adventuring quests or crafters get positioned to do more crafting.

comments.author: AltruisticNostalgia
comments.body: It will definitely change the gaming landscape. It already has now in certain degrees. Especially with Astra as well as Opus 5.5 with their capabilities currently, are moving leaps and bounds. I think with the next one or two iterations of those models, game development will be in the hands of the individual's creative mind.

comments.author: selfVAT
comments.body: Funny part is if you are impressed by Astra wait until you try opus 5.5

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: A faster dev process and more games made in general. I think steam might collapse if it stays anti ai as the percentage goes upward over 70%.

comments.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
comments.body: There's going to be Roblox-like games that use natural language to allow modders / creators of all ages and the first one to catch on with gamers will be huge.

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body: It kind of depends where the ceiling turns out to be.  100 people working with AI can do more than 10 and 1000 people can do more than 100.  At some point, there is a practical ceiling above which more effort and skill doesn’t make sense.  We don’t want games too graphics intensive for the hardware or that take 5,000 hours to complete the story.

comments.author: Ill-Trifle3014
comments.body: Penis simulator

comments.body: [removed]

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: the same with any place that is flooded with content. it will increase trash by leaps and bounds and sometimes create superb stuff we wouldnt see without ai.

comments.author: Dangerous_Serve_4454
comments.body: Honestly I'm more worried about what AI will do to the world in 10 years more than gaming.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Many great and terrible games that would never had been made otherwise.

comments.author: teapot_RGB_color
comments.body:
I think its going to change a lot is conventional workflow, and people need to start thinking outside the box again. But time if adapting is around 10 years so.. I think not that much will be visible from the outside. 

I already see people trying to squeeze it into existing workflows that is designed for hands on and manual work. 

Then it will be another 5 years of development time, so I think not that much will be different.

You would mostly see indie production at near AAA of content. So AAA will have to capture marketing even harder. Basically a repeat of what happened to the music industry when digital production became accessible. (a hostile takeover of media channels)

comments.author: FlightFit335
comments.body: The irony is... terrible games exist now.  How many people buy every game on Steam?  No one so if a game is terrible... who cares.  The kicker is supply will bring down the cost of games.  New platforms will emerge and competition for game distribution will grow.

comments.author: antonation
comments.body: I think games will be models actually and they will be capable of keeping their own internal state and generate scenes and mechanics in real time, there are already some research models that do things like this.

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body: The possibilities of what AI can do for gaming in 10 years are endless. But it's a shame AI in general is going to end society in 5-6 lol

comments.author: Such--Balance
comments.body: Polish, novel ideas and more polish are the only 3 things thats really gonna count.

comments.author: ByteFoundry
comments.body:
I fear nothing positive. The AAA gaming industry is based on the concept of milking their users. This will just increase and accelerate rapidly. With probably mediocre content and ideas.

The demand for games stays more or less constant or grows slowly. AI is increasing supply 1000x as anyone thinks they can make a good enjoyable game. But one idea does not make a good game.  
So the market will be flooded even more than it is  already. 

Finding a good game in that pile of mediocre or bad games is a chance of luck. It already is.  
Marketing will become an even larger pain in the ass.

And make your own game platforms like Roblox already prove this. They are 99% crappy content.

It also means spending time on updating a game is not lucrative. Rather churn out the next thing instead.

And every time someone comes up with a great unique idea it will be copied instantly and monetized before they can.

or: gaming utopia of only great games build to be enjoyable and not monetised every second.

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
If thing keep progressing like this than in ten years indie and solo dev will be able to make game like witcher 3 alone.

And by make i mean you have deep understanding on what to build and how to direct the tools, not a freaking one shot prompt, or blindly prompting.

But this is only if we have no major breakthrough in gaming 

If someone invent full dive sao like game, than it will all change.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
I think we will have more niche games that don't care about marketability, with low player counts, but those players have their needs fully satisfied. That evolution has already happened with studios -> indie developers, and soon, it will be a lot of one-developer games.

And a lot of slop, of course.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
\- People with great ideas and taste will be able to make incredible games.  
\- Value capture will converge: anything looking valuable will be copied in minutes.  
\- Almost impossible to get noticed without capital (wether is money or audience or else)

comments.author: A1bertson
comments.body: Creativity inflation is inevitable. The industry talents has already inflated but I think it will be much worse. I am not yet sure about the scale of it, but I am inclined towards pessimistic scenario. Our best time to make our dream games and hope for some penny is right now.

comments.author: CubersumGame
comments.body:
I’ve already seen Skyrim mods that give AI capabilities to non-player characters. Now, I’m waiting for the same thing to happen with the original Fallout(1-2) games.

I really hope that in a few years, I’ll be able to play games where dialogue offers far more options and takes a much wider range of world events into account.

And perhaps a new RPG hit lies ahead - one that strikes the right balance between atmosphere and procedural generation. I think that’s the main challenge right now: figuring out how to prevent a character from blurting out things they "shouldn't know," or how to ensure each character maintains a distinct personality. But I believe this is a problem that can be solved technically.

comments.author: Queasy-Form-4261
comments.body: I think it is going to allow creative people with no coding experience to make games better than coders with no creative experience.
